findings.evidence: Read of EpsilonEridani.lean lines 1-143; grep for `Parton.PDF` shows ComplexSpinDensity appears only as the import *inside* itself (ComplexSpinDensity.lean:8) and in the Positivity docstring.
findings.issue: `EpsilonEridani.Particles.Parton.PDF.ComplexSpinDensity` is missing from the root index, which is otherwise an exhaustive alphabetical list of every module (PDF.Basic/Model/MsbarPositivity/Positivity are all there, lines 28-31). The new public surface is therefore not exported by `import EpsilonEridani`, and nothing else aggregates it either: `EpsilonEridani/Particles/Parton/Basic.lean:8-9` imports only PDF.Basic and PDF.Positivity.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:139 `lemma diag_nonneg {A : Matrix n n R} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {i : n} : 0 ≤ A i i` — no finiteness hypothesis; the PR already relies on it at PosSemidef.lean:147-148. Repo-wide grep for `psdTestVector|quadraticForm_` matches only PosSemidef.lean.
findings.fix: Prove `apply_self_nonneg` as `hM.diag_nonneg` (dropping `[Finite n]`, as was done for `two_mul_abs_apply_le`) or delete it in favour of Mathlib's `diag_nonneg` and update the four call sites in Positivity.lean:169-187; then delete the test-vector definitions and lemmas and their Main-results entries.
findings.issue: After rewriting `two_mul_abs_apply_le` as a one-line specialisation (line 197-199), the public test-vector machinery — `psdTestVector`, `sum_mul_psdTestVector`, `sum_psdTestVector_mul`, `PosSemidef.quadraticForm_nonneg`, `PosSemidef.quadraticForm_psdTestVector` — has no consumer left in the repo except `apply_self_nonneg`, which is itself Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef.diag_nonneg` with a redundant `[Finite n]`. The docstring still advertises two of them as Main results (lines 43-44). This is a duplicated/obsolete public surface created by this PR's own refactor.

findings.evidence: ComplexSpinDensity.lean:173-184 defines the predicate and two diagonal eliminators only; no lemma in the file mentions both `IsParityInvariant` and `toSpinDensity`/`toSpinDensityC`.
findings.fix: Add `IsParityInvariant.toSpinDensity : ρ.IsParityInvariant → (ρ.toSpinDensity h).IsParityInvariant` (the converse fails and should be said so), and an `isParityInvariant_def`/`_iff` restatement so the predicate is usable without unfolding.
findings.issue: `SpinDensityC.IsParityInvariant` gets no characteristic restatement and no transport across the real/complex bridge, while `IsTimeReversalInvariant` gets two (`isTimeReversalInvariant_iff_forall_im_eq_zero`, `isTimeReversalInvariant_iff_transpose_eq`). Since the complex predicate is strictly stronger than the identically-named `SpinDensity.IsParityInvariant` (Positivity.lean:227, diagonal only) and the file documents that difference at line 170, a consumer holding complex parity cannot reach `f1_eq_of_parityInvariant` on the real side without unfolding both defs.

findings.evidence: Positivity.lean:168, 179, 210 state all three bounds for the real matrix; ComplexSpinDensity.lean states only `soffer_bound`. `Matrix.PosSemidef.diag_nonneg` (mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:139) gives `0 ≤ ρ.mat i i` in `ℂ`, whose `re` is the needed real bound — the same route the PR uses at PosSemidef.lean:147.
findings.fix: Add `f1_nonneg : 0 ≤ ρ.f1` and `abs_deltaQ_le_f1 : |ρ.deltaQ| ≤ ρ.f1`, from `ρ.posSemidef.diag_nonneg` through `f1_add_deltaQ`/`f1_sub_deltaQ`, mirroring Positivity.lean:168-191.
findings.issue: `soffer_bound` is proved for `SpinDensityC` but the two cheaper siblings of the real module — `f1_nonneg` (`0 ≤ f1`) and `abs_g1_le_f1` (`|deltaQ| ≤ f1`) — are not. They do not transport from the real side for a general (non-T-invariant) `SpinDensityC`, so a consumer of `f1`/`deltaQ` has no nonnegativity lemma at all. `f1_sub_deltaQ` (line 143) is stated with no consumer and is exactly the ingredient for the second.

summary: The new module is never added to the library root index, so `SpinDensityC` is not reachable from `import EpsilonEridani`; and the PosSemidef refactor leaves a now-unused public test-vector machinery whose only remaining consumer duplicates Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef.diag_nonneg`. Two smaller API gaps: no bridge or characteristic lemma for `IsParityInvariant`, and no complex analogues of `f1_nonneg`/`abs_g1_le_f1`.
